details.note: The attacker lists the partners from the firm's website and probes its remote-access portal.
They register a domain one letter off a client's and build an invoice document with a malicious macro.
The invoice arrives by email, addressed by name to the accounts team.
A clerk enables editing and the macro runs a script.
The script installs a backdoor that survives a restart.
The backdoor calls home every few minutes for instructions.
They copy client files, delete the backups, then encrypt the file server and demand payment.

name: Kill chain
note: Each event is one stage of an attack, in order, following a ransomware attack on a small law firm. Under each stage, write what your logs would show and the control that breaks the chain there; the earlier you break it, the cheaper it is.
outline: Break: disable macros from the internet
Watch: regular beacons to new domains
Break: filter outbound DNS and web
summary: Seven stages to spot and break
title: Ransomware at a law firm
